articles.title: Ivete Sangalo beija novo namorado durante show e surpreende fãs | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantora baiana apresentava a música 'Em Busca da Minha Sorte', quando desceu as escadas do palco e viveu momento romântico com o produtor musical Tiago Maia.
articles.summary: Cantora baiana apresentava a música 'Em Busca da Minha Sorte', quando desceu as escadas do palco e viveu momento romântico com o produtor musical Tiago Maia
articles.body:
A cantora baiana Ivete Sangalo beijou o novo namorado, o produtor musical Tiago Maia , e surpreendeu os fãs que acompanhavam um show da turnê "Clareou", em Fortaleza (CE).

A apresentação aconteceu no sábado (10), reunindo uma multidão. Enquanto cantava "Em Busca da Minha Sorte", a baiana desceu as escadas da passarela montada no palco e foi ao encontro do amado.

Um vídeo feito por uma das pessoas presentes mostra o momento. Sem esperar a atitude, o público ovacionou a artista e reagiu com palmas ao ato de carinho. (Assista acima)

Nas redes sociais, fãs aproveitaram para deixar mensagens de carinho para o casal. "Ele com vergonha. Vivendo e amando", comentou uma internauta. "Todo amor do mundo para eles", escreveu outra.

Ivete Sangalo beija novo namorado durante show e surpreende fãs — Foto: Central do Axé

Ivete Sangalo e o nutricionista Daniel Cady anunciaram a separação em novembro do ano passado , depois de 14 anos de casamento.

Os dois têm três filhos: o primogênito Marcelo, de 16 anos, e as gêmeas Marina e Helena, de 7. Eles continuam morando com a mãe, mas sempre convivem com o pai.

A cantora e Tiago Maia só começaram a ser vistos juntos em 2026. O produtor musical é catarinense e também é empresário.

articles.title: Will hit streets again until PM Modi’s dictatorship ends, says CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke
articles.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke vows to resume protests until Modi “dictatorship” ends; alleges Delhi Police rights violations, harassment and denied legal access.
articles.body: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday said his agitation would continue until what he called Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “dictatorship” came to an end.Speaking to the reporters following his recent arrest, Dipke accused the Delhi Police of mentally harassing him, violating his fundamental rights and preventing him from contacting his lawyer and family.“We will continue our agitation until Narendra Modi’s dictatorship ends. We will soon return to the streets,” Dipke said, reiterating his resolve to continue the protest despite the police action.Dipke’s mother, Anita, said the family would never forget how the govt’s actions prevented her son from seeing his grandmother for the last time. “We will not forget this until our last breath. Because of this govt, Abhijeet could not see his grandmother for the last time,” she said.Abhijeet alleged that Delhi Police violated his legal rights during his arrest by denying him access to his lawyer and brother. He challenged police to release the complete, unedited video of the arrest, claiming authorities withheld his whereabouts and details of the police station where he was detained from his family and legal representatives for an entire day.Abhijeet also alleged that the police subjected him to mental harassment at a time when his grandmother had died. “At around 3.30am, the police brought the arrest papers to me and pressured me to sign them, saying that I would be in jail for a long time and should call my parents and inform them,” he claimed, describing the episode as mental harassment of both him and his family.He also criticised the police for allegedly deploying women personnel during the arrest. Claiming that the move was intended to protect male officers from allegations of misconduct, Dipke said he and his associates were educated and knew how to treat women with respect. His allegations against Delhi Police could not be independently verified.Responding to questions about the possibility of externment from Maharashtra, Dipke targeted chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, questioning the state govt’s intentions and its handling of the issue.Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. articles.title: Central Delhi swells with protesters as India bloc holds march seeking CEC’s removal
articles.summary: INDIA bloc’s Chalo Dilli march led by Rahul Gandhi draws thousands in central Delhi, seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal and opposing electoral roll SIR.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Around 5:30 pm, Bhagwan Das Road was packed with people streaming in from the Mandi House side. Some were perched on trees and some sat on buses, waving flags as INDIA bloc politicians passed by on a truck. A little ahead, at the end of the road, cops stood behind barricades blocking the stretch leading to Tilak Lane. As they secured the barriers with a rope, hundreds of police and paramilitary personnel advanced towards the gathering.On Monday, INDIA Bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli-March for Democracy’, led by Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, brought thousands into central Delhi, turning roads between Connaught Place and Supreme Court into a sea of supporters waving flags and shouting slogans. The alliance was demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR of electoral rolls over allegations of irregularities.The gathering had begun building hours earlier. By 1.30 pm, Barakhamba Road, which was closed to traffic, was full of opposition supporters and protesters. Some climbed onto buses and waved their flags above the crowd while waiting for Rahul and other alliance members.Around 3.30 pm, Rahul arrived with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other members of the alliance in a bus, which first approached Barakhamba Road from the Mandi House side, took a U-turn near Statesman House and headed back towards Mandi House as supporters marched in solidarity.Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee visited Constitution Club to express “solidarity” before leaving for Kolkata.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav were among those present. The bus also carried K C Venugopal, Tejashwi Yadav, Supriya Sule, Dipankar Bhattacharya, Sanjay Raut, MA Baby, D Raja, DK Shivakumar, Revanth Reddy, Dharmendra Yadav, Sachin Pilot, Abhishek Singhvi, Saugata Roy, V Sivadasan and Deepender Hooda, along with Yogendra Yadav, Neha Bora and Sai Balaji.Rahul, Priyanka and Bora then got off the bus and began walking together, with thousands following. Members of student organisations and civil society groups as well as youth activists joined opposition supporters, their cheers accompanying the march towards Supreme Court.“Vote chor, gaddi chhor” echoed along the stretch. Another chant, “Ek kachori, do samosa, in teeno ka kya bharosa”, seemed to target PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah and the CEC. Some turned up wearing Batman masks, referencing a viral meme depicting Rahul as the superhero.The procession had travelled only a short distance when police stopped it. Near Barakhamba Road, demonstrators pushed through barricades as cops tried to push them back. Rahul was subsequently seen atop a truck with Akhilesh, Tejashwi, Venugopal and Sule, among others.On Bhagwan Das Road, many climbed onto a line of parked police vehicles and buses, shouting and cheering as the INDIA bloc members waved back at them. Flags of NSUI, Youth Congress, AISA, AISF and SP fluttered above the crowd.Police then began directing the supporters to one side. People started pushing and pulling as security personnel — officers said more than 10,000 personnel had been deployed in and around New Delhi — moved into the crowd.Amid this, the truck carrying the politicians took a U-turn and headed in the opposite direction, while the protesters began scattering. Later, the politicians reached Supreme Court and a petition was filed naming Election Commission of India as a respondent. The plea challenges the decisions taken related to the SIR of electoral rolls and calls for transparency and safeguards against voter deletions.The march followed CJI Surya Kant’s decision to decline a meeting sought by opposition members to submit a memorandum on alleged electoral irregularities. Citing proceedings already pending before the court, he advised them to raise their concerns through a formal petition.Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee president Devender Yadav said, “As long as this vote thief (CEC Kumar) does not step down, this movement will continue”. He added, “We have been fighting this battle for a long time. But BJP has been protecting the CEC as he acts at the behest of Modi and Shah to indulge in malpractices to steal elections by robbing people’s verdict. From now on, he won’t be allowed to misuse his position. He has committed anti-national and anti-people sins from which he cannot escape. articles.title: As Jantar Mantar loses protest site tag, CJP plans get disrupted
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Monday gave Delhi Police 24 hours to set a date for its proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against alleged electoral
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Monday gave Delhi Police 24 hours to set a date for its proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against alleged electoral roll revision irregularities, offering the force the choice to decide when it could be held.However, just as the green light was sought, police announced the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, throwing CJP's plan into uncertainty and prompting it to slam the move.Hours before party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka came to Parliament Street police station to submit a letter regarding its demand, barricades and security personnel had taken over adjacent roads.Even Firoz Shah Road, around 10 minutes away, had barricades and police personnel stationed along it.Closer to Parliament Street, access was restricted, with loudspeakers repeatedly warning: "Section 163 of BNSS is in place. Please abide by law and order. Stay away from barricades on the road." Just outside the police station, security was even tighter, with announcements also spelling out restrictions for media personnel.Ranka said, "We have come to police with a letter giving them the option to suggest a date on which we can hold our protest. The DCP came into the room, but left when he saw us sitting there. So, we could not meet him. The additional DCP and SHO are not present. It appears the entire police station has been vacated since CJP members arrived. Anyway, we have submitted the letter."In its communication, CJP claimed that over 55,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across Delhi over the past three days, disrupting normal life.It alleged arbitrary detentions, physical aggression and prolonged custody involving common people and journalists, besides flagging financial losses suffered by businesses forced to down shutters.The party blamed road closures, barricades and the refusal to allot Jantar Mantar as a protest site for growing public distress. It demanded a scaling down of security deployment, an end to alleged illegal detentions and harassment of independent journalists, and permission to protest at a designated site.Das said, "Protesting peacefully is our democratic right. What happened in the past day (was akin to govt) waging a war against its own citizens."The party said that students, youth and other citizens cannot be prevented from exercising their constitutional right to assemble and protest peacefully.Soon after Jantar Mantar's denotification was announced, Ranka posted on social media, "Why not declare Mt Everest as the designated protest site? Thirty minutes after we went to Delhi Police asking for a date when we can go to Jantar Mantar, it was denotified."CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke wrote on social media, "Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar... Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself... Anyway, Jantar Mantar was turned into a war zone... Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!"Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Incêndios no Amazonas: Emergência em 36 cidades e aulas suspensas | G1
articles.standfirst: Situação de emergência foi reconhecida em 36 dos 62 municípios do estado. Investigações apontam incêndios criminosos, enquanto a fumaça afeta a saúde da população e provoca a suspensão de atividades.
articles.summary: O governo reconheceu emergência em 36 cidades devido aos incêndios no Amazonas, que provocam fumaça intensa, suspendem aulas e afetam a saúde dos moradores.
articles.body:
Os incêndios florestais já colocaram 36 dos 62 municípios do Amazonas , mais da metade do estado , em situação de emergência . A crise provocada pelo avanço do fogo e pela fumaça levou à suspensão de aulas , à paralisação de atividades ao ar livre , ao envio de alertas de saúde à população e ao reforço das operações de combate às queimadas em diversas regiões do estado.

As investigações também apontam que há incêndios criminosos no estado . Em Itacoatiara , no interior do Amazonas, oito suspeitos de provocar queimadas na zona rural foram identificados em apurações conduzidas pela Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente (Semma). Os casos foram encaminhados à Polícia Civil e ao Ministério Público do Amazonas (MPAM).

Durante um sobrevoo de monitoramento nas áreas atingidas, uma comitiva do governo federal identificou diversos focos de incêndio dentro de áreas de mata nativa preservada e em locais isolados , de difícil acesso.

O ministro do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima do Brasil João Paulo Capobianco afirmou que o cenário indica ação humana intencional . O órgão alertou para a possibilidade de uso do fogo para degradar a floresta e preparar áreas para o desmatamento ilegal .

O ministro também defendeu o combate à impunidade e a atuação conjunta da Polícia Militar, de outras forças policiais, do Corpo de Bombeiros e de agentes federais para identificar e responsabilizar os envolvidos.

"É fundamental que esses indivíduos que estão agindo criminosamente vejam que serão punidos. Ou seja, é necessário combater a impunidade que está reinando aqui na região", alertou.

O g1 procurou o Governo do Amazonas e a Secretaria de Segurança Pública do estado (SSP-AM) para saber se a Polícia Militar já estava atuando no combate aos incêndios criminosos, mas não obteve retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

Governo federal reconhece emergência em 36 municípios

O reconhecimento da situação de emergência nos 36 municípios afetados foi oficializado pelo Ministério da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional (MIDR) no sábado (10). A medida permite a atuação integrada das forças de resposta e o repasse de recursos federais .

O ministro da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional, Waldez Góes, destacou que a medida ajuda tanto no combate aos incêndios quanto na assistência à população atingida.

"Uma coisa é enfrentar em todas as frentes e empregar toda a força que puder, Governo Federal junto com o Estado e municípios, para apagar o fogo. A outra é assistir pessoas que já estão, de alguma forma, precisando de ajuda humanitária, de assistência médica como resultado do incêndio", afirmou.

Também no sábado, chegaram a Manaus aeronaves de combate a incêndios, entre elas aviões Air Tractor e helicópteros do Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama), além de 290 brigadistas federais.

No domingo (11), a fumaça reduziu a visibilidade e atrasou a decolagem da comitiva ministerial que faria um sobrevoo de monitoramento em Manaus . Após visitar áreas críticas, como a região de Autazes , o ministro do Meio Ambiente classificou a situação como "mais grave do que eu imaginava" ao encontrar incêndios dentro de floresta preservada.

No mesmo dia, uma força-tarefa enviada pelo governo de São Paulo embarcou com 30 especialistas, entre bombeiros e agentes da Defesa Civil, além de drones e 11 mil litros de retardante de chamas.

Já na segunda-feira (12), o governo federal começou a enviar alertas de emergência pelo WhatsApp, por meio da conta oficial GovBR . As mensagens orientavam os moradores sobre o uso de máscaras, a vedação de imóveis para reduzir a entrada de fumaça e a importância da hidratação .

Nas operações aéreas, o cargueiro KC-390 Millennium, da Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB), realizou missões de combate aos incêndios , com capacidade para lançar até 12 mil litros de água por voo. Aviões do Ibama também lançaram mais de 10 mil litros de água na Região Metropolitana de Manaus.

Fumaça suspende aulas nas redes municipal, estadual e federal

A fumaça que encobre Manaus provocou a suspensão de aulas em diferentes instituições de ensino. A Prefeitura de Manaus manteve a suspensão das atividades da rede municipal nesta terça-feira (13) . Já a Secretaria de Estado de Educação e Desporto Escolar (Seduc) suspendeu as aulas nos turnos matutino, vespertino e noturno nas escolas da capital .

A suspensão também vale para as escolas estaduais de Autazes e do distrito de Cacau Pirêra , em Iranduba , em todos os turnos . Segundo a Seduc, as medidas buscam evitar a exposição da comunidade escolar à fumaça intensa.

A secretaria informou que acompanha diariamente a situação em Manaus e nos demais municípios afetados. As escolas também podem reduzir o tempo das aulas ou suspender atividades, caso necessário.

As medidas seguem orientações da Nota Técnica Conjunta nº 22/2026 da Secretaria de Estado de Saúde do Amazonas (SES-AM) e da Fundação de Vigilância em Saúde do Amazonas Dra. Rosemary Costa Pinto (FVS-RCP). O documento recomenda reduzir a exposição à fumaça, suspender atividades físicas e pedagógicas ao ar livre e manter ambientes internos fechados sempre que possível.

No Instituto Federal do Amazonas ( Ifam ), o Campus Manaus Centro suspendeu, nesta terça-feira, as aulas e demais atividades acadêmicas e administrativas presenciais em todos os turnos.

Fumaça também interrompe competições de base

Segundo a entidade, a decisão foi tomada devido à intensa presença de fumaça na atmosfera, que compromete a qualidade do ar e representa riscos à saúde.

"Diante desse contexto, a FAF entende que a preservação da saúde e da integridade física de atletas, comissões técnicas, profissionais da arbitragem e demais envolvidos nas competições deve ser prioridade", informou a federação.

Manaus segue com a pior qualidade do ar do Brasil

Apesar da chuva registrada durante a madrugada desta terça-feira, Manaus continuou com a pior qualidade do ar do Brasil , segundo a plataforma internacional IQAir.

No interior, Autazes registrou o maior número de focos de queimadas nas últimas 72 horas . Foram 139 ocorrências, o equivalente a 19,1% de todos os registros do estado no período. A qualidade do ar no município foi classificada como péssima .

Focos de queimadas aumentam 271% em outubro

Incêndio de grandes proporções na região do Rio Urubu, na zona rural de Itacoatiara, interior do Amazonas — Foto: Liam Cavalcante/Rede Amazônica

Dados do Painel do Fogo, do Centro Gestor e Operacional do Sistema de Proteção da Amazônia (Censipam), e do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe) mostram o aumento das queimadas no estado.

Nos dez primeiros dias de outubro, o Amazonas registrou 1.380 focos de incêndio , alta de 271% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025, quando foram contabilizados 372 focos.

A maior parte dos registros, 1.186 , ocorreu em áreas públicas. Também foram identificados 246 focos em assentamentos federais, 116 em terras indígenas e 97 em unidades de conservação.

Quatro municípios amazonenses aparecem entre os 20 com mais focos de queimadas no Brasil em outubro:

Lábrea: 214 focos, na 4ª posição nacional;

O cenário também mostra uma mudança nas regiões mais atingidas. Diferentemente de anos anteriores, quando o Sul do Amazonas concentrava o maior número de queimadas, os incêndios passaram a atingir com força a Região Metropolitana de Manaus e o Baixo Amazonas .

A mudança é atribuída à instalação de bases permanentes do Corpo de Bombeiros no Sul do estado.

A fumaça tem prejudicado a rotina dos moradores , que relatam irritação na garganta, congestão nasal, dores de cabeça e dificuldade para dormir.

Em Manaus, foram registrados 82 atendimentos de urgência por problemas respiratórios atribuídos à fumaça entre os dias 1º e 8 de outubro , segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde do Amazonas (SES-AM).

No interior, os incêndios também provocaram prejuízos à vegetação e à produção agrícola . Na zona rural de Itacoatiara, na comunidade do Jacarezinho, o fogo destruiu 256,71 hectares de vegetação , área equivalente a cerca de 360 campos de futebol.

Em Parintins , a destruição de lavouras provocou desabastecimento de produtos agrícolas e aumento de até 100% no preço de derivados da mandioca, como a farinha.

Força-tarefa reúne 11 aeronaves e 290 brigadistas

Para conter o avanço das chamas, o governo federal mobilizou 11 aeronaves e 290 brigadistas do Ibama, do Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade ( ICMBio ) e da Força Nacional.

Seis aviões Air Tractor: utilizados para lançar água diretamente sobre os focos de incêndio em Autazes, no entorno de Manaus e em Itacoatiara.

Um cargueiro KC-390 Millennium, da FAB : usado para lançar grandes volumes de água na região do Baixo Amazonas, incluindo áreas próximas a Parintins e Itacoatiara.

Três helicópteros e um avião Caravana: destinados ao transporte de brigadistas, equipamentos e apoio logístico.

A distribuição das aeronaves prevê atuação em diferentes áreas do estado, incluindo Autazes, Manaus, Itacoatiara e Parintins. Os helicópteros também ficam disponíveis para diferentes missões operacionais. Além disso, o planejamento inclui a estruturação de uma base de apoio às operações aéreas em Itacoatiara.

Na terça-feira (13), a previsão é que o cargueiro faça mais três voos : um na região de Parintins e dois em Itacoatiara.

articles.title: TikTok star Becca Bloom teases never-before-shared personal stories ahead of January 2027 podcast launch
articles.summary: TikTok star Becca Bloom is preparing to give fans a closer look at the person behind her popular online persona.
articles.body: TikTok star Becca Bloom is preparing to give fans a closer look at the person behind her popular online persona. The social media creator, who has built a following of more than 10 million across platforms, is stepping into long-form entertainment with a new podcast called “Bloom's Room.” The weekly audio and video series will premiere in January 2027 under Pave Studios’ OpenMind lifestyle brand. Known for discussing money, fashion, relationships and business, Bloom now plans to explore these subjects in greater depth, sharing personal experiences and conversations that go beyond the short clips her audience knows.TikTok star Becca Bloom reveals what fans can expect from ‘Bloom's Room’Bloom has built her online presence by discussing topics that affect everyday decisions, from financial goals to personal relationships. Her upcoming podcast will give her more room to explore these subjects, along with ambition, identity, investing and the psychology behind people's choices.The creator says the new project will also offer a different perspective on her private life. Although millions follow her online, she believes her short videos reveal only a small part of who she is."I'm a relatively private person, and what I've shared online has mostly been 30-second glimpses into my life. If those are the trailers, then 'Bloom's Room' is the movie," Bloom says.She also explained why she wanted to move beyond short-form content and create a space for longer discussions."The things I have the most to say about, and the conversations I think are actually worth having, rarely fit into 30 seconds," Bloom says. "We'll get into money, relationships, fashion, and why we make the choices we do, but also parts of my life and conversations I've never shared publicly."Each episode will focus on a subject Bloom wants to examine more closely. Some installments will draw on her finance background and experience building an online audience, while others will feature guests sharing their knowledge and personal stories.The format could allow Bloom to connect with viewers interested in more than quick advice or glimpses of her lifestyle. It will also give her the opportunity to discuss the difference between earning money and building ownership, alongside the challenges that can come with success.TikTok star Becca Bloom joins Pave Studios’ growing podcast lineupPave Studios is expanding its creator-led programming by partnering with personalities who already have established audiences. The company plans to develop “Bloom's Room” across both audio and video, giving the series a wider format than traditional podcast listening alone.CEO Max Cutler welcomed the partnership, highlighting Bloom's appeal and the audience's interest in learning more about her life beyond social media.“Becca is one of the most compelling voices of her generation, and we’re thrilled to partner with her,” CEO Max Cutler says. “Her audience has always wanted to know more about the person behind the content, and this show creates the space for that. It’s exactly the kind of creator-led original OpenMind was built for, and we can’t wait for people to hear the conversations she’s going to have.”The January 2027 launch will add to OpenMind's growing slate, which includes “Khloé in Wonder Land,” hosted by Khloé Kardashian. Pave Studios also operates Crime House, which focuses on true crime, and Rewind, a history-focused brand.For Bloom, the new series marks a shift from brief social media updates to deeper conversations. Whether discussing financial decisions, relationships or personal ambition, she will have a new platform to share ideas that need more than a few seconds to explain.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'We are not happy': Trump likely to fire Greece ambassador Guilfoyle after misconduct reports
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday said he was “looking at” firing US ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle after several reports alleged that she had
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Monday said he was “looking at” firing US ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle after several reports alleged that she had engaged in improper and possibly illegal conduct before and during her tenure in Athens.“Well, we’re looking at it,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “We’re not happy.”This comes after The Wall Street Journal reported questionable conduct by Guilfoyle, including allegedly threatening a host-country official, accepting improper gifts and services, and offering to use her influence within the administration in exchange for payment of a large credit card bill.Guilfoyle has not directly addressed the reports, but in a statement released late Sunday, her lawyers denied that she had done anything wrong. They claimed that the money she was seeking from a Trump donor was payment for services, including public appearances and speaking engagements, that predated her nomination as ambassador and for which she had not been paid.“Ambassador Guilfoyle has served, and will continue to serve, with integrity, honor and distinction. We are evaluating all available legal remedies to collect this debt and any other potential causes of action,” her lawyers said.Since late September, the Journal has detailed several accounts of questionable conduct by Guilfoyle.Its first report said she had told guests at a reception that the US could undermine the Greek government if it chose to, promoted the business interests of a particular Greek construction and energy company, and allowed the company's lobbyist to attend private diplomatic meetings.The Journal later reported that Guilfoyle had been enraged at not being invited to a Greek-themed event at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, earlier this year. She allegedly demanded to attend while boasting about luxury travel to France with energy company executives.Another report, by British tabloid The Daily Mail, said Guilfoyle had alienated staff at the US Embassy in Athens and pushed the boundaries of behaviour appropriate for the top representative of the US government in Greece.Guilfoyle is a former Fox News Channel host and California prosecutor. articles.title: California raises soil saturation to 90% using artificial seeps at Camp Pendleton to restore endangered Willow Flycatcher habitat, but eight passing birds and no nests are recorded
articles.summary: California’s efforts to restore habitat for the endangered Southwestern Willow Flycatcher at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton include artificial seeps and
articles.body: California’s efforts to restore habitat for the endangered Southwestern Willow Flycatcher at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton include artificial seeps and birdsong broadcasts designed to encourage breeding. According to the US Geological Survey report, seep sites had higher soil saturation than nearby reference areas in 2025, although significant improvements were not recorded across all vegetation measures. Surveys detected eight transient Willow Flycatchers of unknown subspecies, but no resident birds or nesting activity. Researchers also documented non-native plants and damage to willow and sycamore trees associated with invasive shothole borer infestations, highlighting continuing challenges for habitat restoration and the species’ recovery.How do artificial seeps improve Willow Flycatcher habitatCamp Pendleton began operating an artificial seep along the Santa Margarita River in 2019 as part of a habitat enhancement project associated with the Conjunctive Use Project. Two additional seeps were installed in early 2021, bringing the total to three. The pumps were designed to draw shallow groundwater to the surface during daylight hours, generally from around mid-April to the end of August, to improve conditions in areas used historically by breeding Willow Flycatchers.Surface water and saturated soil are important components of Willow Flycatcher habitat. Researchers established permanent vegetation sampling locations in 2025 to assess the effects of the seeps and compare them with nearby reference sites without artificial seeps. The study included 48 vegetation sampling locations across the seep and reference areas. Although pump operation was affected by maintenance issues, soil saturation remained significantly higher at seep sites than at reference sites during the study.How did artificial seeps affect soil saturation and vegetationThe 2025 assessment found average soil saturation of 90 per cent at seep sites, compared with 30 per cent at reference sites. Researchers also reported that non-native vegetation cover was higher at reference sites than at seep sites across the measured height categories. These findings documented differences in moisture conditions and some vegetation characteristics associated with the artificial seep project.However, the report did not find significant differences between seep and reference sites in total vegetation cover, woody vegetation cover, total herbaceous cover or native herbaceous cover. Researchers also found no significant differences in average or maximum canopy height between the two site types. The results therefore did not demonstrate that increased soil saturation had translated directly into all the vegetation conditions associated with suitable breeding habitat.How did researchers find eight transient Willow FlycatchersEight transient Willow Flycatchers were observed during surveys conducted between May and July 2025. Seven were detected along the Santa Margarita River and one along Las Flores Creek. No Willow Flycatchers were detected at Fallbrook, Pilgrim or San Mateo creeks. The birds were observed in mixed willow and riparian scrub habitats, and researchers did not observe nesting during the 2025 breeding season.Exotic vegetation was present at most locations where transient flycatchers were detected, and poison hemlock was the most common non-native plant recorded in those locations. Researchers also observed dead and declining willow and sycamore trees associated with an ongoing invasive shothole borer infestation. The report identifies continued operation of artificial seeps, further assessment of vegetation changes and continued use of vocalisation broadcasts as measures that could contribute to future recovery efforts.You use AI every day. articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday criticised Yemen’s Houthi rebels over their escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying the group was “misbehaving very
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Monday criticised Yemen’s Houthi rebels over their escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying the group was “misbehaving very badly”.“The Houthis are misbehaving very badly. No good,” Trump told reporters when asked what the United States would do about the group.Asked whether the Houthi attacks had intensified in connection with the US midterm elections, Trump said, “I don't know how it affects the election. I don't take that into account.”“I just know Iran will never have a nuclear weapon... They're never going to have a nuclear weapon. But the Houthis are misbehaving,” he added.His remarks come amid a series of attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, including strikes involving Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.Trump had earlier said Washington would consider joining Saudi Arabia in military operations against the Houthis following the latest attack on King Khalid International Airport.“We just found out about the recent attack - we'll make a decision,” Trump told reporters at the White House on Saturday, adding, “We're going to take a look.”Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition on Tuesday said it had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi militia towards the Khamis Mushait airbase in Saudi Arabia.In a post on X, coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki said: “Interception and destruction of two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Khamis Mushait.”Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence agency had earlier urged residents of Khamis Mushait Governorate to remain vigilant over a potential threat. In a subsequent post on X, it said the danger had passed and asked residents to continue following safety instructions and avoid gathering or filming. It also provided 998 as the emergency helpline.The interception came after Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed that the group's forces had targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile and carried out a drone operation against Khamis Mushait airbase.On October 10, 13 people, including an Indian national, were killed and hundreds injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport. Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) had initially reported 12 fatalities and 309 injuries in a statement issued on October 11. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh later confirmed the death of an Indian national who had been injured in the attack.A series of attacks also targeted King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7, leaving three people dead and 36 injured, according to GACA. Airport operations were temporarily suspended as authorities assessed the damage and conducted safety inspections in coordination with relevant agencies.You use AI every day. articles.body: Tectone has raised concerns about streamer Reggie, also known as Lil Rodney Son, following his allegations against Kai Cenat and other members of the Clover Boys. On October 12, the streamer said Reggie’s recent behaviour could lead to suicide if nobody checked on him. His comments came amid an ongoing dispute that began in late September, when Reggie accused Cenat of grooming 17-year-old streamer RaKai and claimed the Twitch star had too much influence over the platform. The allegations remain unverified, and both Cenat and RaKai have rejected claims made against them.Tectone Raises Suicide Concern Over Reggie’s Allegations Against Kai CenatTectone addressed Reggie’s actions in a post on X, describing his behaviour as a possible “drug induced crash out”. He expressed concern about where the situation might lead if people close to Reggie did not step in.“I’m telling you this Reggie drug-induced crash-out is gonna lead to his suicide if someone doesn’t check on him.”Tectone followed that warning with another remark about Reggie’s state of mind, writing, “Obviously this dude is going crazy.”His comments came as Reggie continued to speak publicly about his fallout with Cenat and the Clover Boys. The dispute has included serious allegations about Cenat’s conduct towards RaKai, as well as claims that Cenat could affect other creators’ careers on Twitch. However, these claims have not been independently established.Cenat has denied the accusations and threatened legal action against Reggie. During his response, he challenged Reggie to provide evidence, asking, “Where is your proof?” He later said, “I’m suing you, bro!”RaKai has also denied being sexually abused while growing up. His response is important because Reggie’s allegations included claims involving the younger streamer. Neither Reggie’s accusations against Cenat nor his claims about the wider group should be treated as proven facts.Reggie Targets Kai Cenat and Clover Boys in Instagram StoriesReggie returned to the dispute on October 11, sharing several Instagram Stories that included photos of himself getting his hair done, recording music and commenting on the group. One post discussed how much money different Clover Boys members had, while also questioning whether Brazilian streamer Tota had officially belonged to the group.“All pocket watching aside: Rakai got the most money in clover anybody can see that then it’s Ray then it’s Tylil then it’s me then it’s dez then it’s punga ‘tbh tota was never a official member’ -KC3.”Reggie also said his experience at the Clover House had caused him trauma, arguing that viewers did not know what happened when cameras were switched off.“Stop saying Kai and The Clover Boys ain’t cause me Trauma cus yall wasn’t behind them mansion walls with me when that camera cut off yall only know what yall see. Nothing is what it seems all ts fake.”He then accused Cenat of trying to damage his career and warned that he would continue speaking out.“That man tried to shelf my career he going hear from me until they silence me and to my brother you put ya self in a wild predicament by posting your self, be safe everyone.”The comments were reported by Sportskeeda on October 12, citing Reggie’s Instagram Stories and Tectone’s post. The public dispute continues, with Cenat threatening legal action and Reggie standing by his allegations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bunkers, handpicked guards: How Saudi Prince MBS moves between palaces amid Houthi threat
articles.summary: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is moving between heavily guarded palaces equipped with bunkers as the kingdom faces renewed Houthi attacks amid
articles.body: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is moving between heavily guarded palaces equipped with bunkers as the kingdom faces renewed Houthi attacks amid the wider conflict linked to the Iran war, as reported by the Wall Street Journal.The crown prince’s last public appearance was on Tuesday, when he donated blood as part of a national donation drive.The 41-year-old crown prince is being protected by a handpicked security team, officials familiar with his movements said, as reported by Wall Street Journal.Saudi Arabia is struggling to shield key infrastructure and economic assets from further Houthi aattacks.At least one Houthi missile struck Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday, killing at least 12 people and injuring hundreds, many of them seriously. It was the deadliest attack on the United States or its Gulf allies in conflicts linked to the Iran war.The Houthis have struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh at least four times.Prince Mohammed brought Saudi Arabia into Yemen’s civil war in 2015, backing the internationally recognised government against the Houthis. The Saudi-led intervention involved devastating airstrikes that intensified the conflict and fuelled the Houthis’ campaign against the kingdom, including attacks on oil facilities and cities such as Riyadh.The two sides fought to a stalemate before agreeing to a ceasefire in 2022.The latest outbreak of violence comes as Prince Mohammed seeks to contain the confrontation with Iran. Attacks launched by Tehran early in the war exposed the vulnerability of energy facilities and economic assets, including airports, across the Gulf.Saudi Arabia is also struggling to provide air defence coverage across its vast territory. The kingdom has been shifting air defence batteries to protect palaces and energy infrastructure, people familiar with its deliberations said.Saudi Arabia is also seeking a more direct US role in countering Houthi attacks. Washington has provided intelligence sharing, target identification and planning support for a Saudi-led offensive but has so far refrained from launching strikes against the rebels.US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he was considering military action against the Houthis following the deadly attack on Riyadh’s international airport.However, US intervention could widen the conflict and threaten a critical global shipping route. The Houthis could attempt to disrupt traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden near Yemen.Such a disruption could further restrict global oil supplies, already affected by Iran’s efforts to choke off the Strait of Hormuz. Before the US-Iran war began, about one-fifth of the world’s oil passed through the strategic waterway.The Houthis seized key areas along the Bab el-Mandeb last month. The Saudi-led coalition, which backs forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognised government, has been trying to retake those areas.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court registry Monday flagged 14 defects in a petition filed by the Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court registry Monday flagged 14 defects in a petition filed by the Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the special intensive revision of electoral rolls.The registry asked the lawyer who filed the petition to submit a clear copy of the identity card of Congress chief and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge, one of the co-petitioners, news agency PTI reported.The registry also flagged illegible or missing pages in the petition. It further pointed out a shortfall of Rs 220 in the court fee.Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut responded to the Supreme Court registry flagging defects in the opposition bloc's petition, saying the INDIA bloc remained determined to hold the constitutional body accountable.Speaking to news agency ANI about the technical discrepancies in the petition, Raut said, "The petition that has been filed mentions that the fee is short by Rs 220, there are several errors, and there are facts about 14 documents mentioned in it. Well, it is possible. We have individual petitions in the names of Rahul Ji, Mallikarjun Kharge Ji, and all other India Bloc leaders. There might be some errors in it, which we will now rectify and repair."Confirming his participation in the legal challenge, Raut said, "Definitely, I am a petitioner. All the parties that were involved in yesterday's protest are all petitioners."On Monday, Rahul and several other opposition leaders marched to the Supreme Court to file the petition.The INDIA bloc leaders, led by Rahul Gandhi and joined by thousands of supporters, sought scrutiny of the Election Commission's functioning, measures to prevent CEC Gyanesh Kumar from taking decisions "unilaterally", alleged "arbitrary" voter deletions during SIR, and the system governing the use and deployment of electronic voting machines (EVMs).The petitioners included Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC's Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav, RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, Sena (UBT)'s Sanjay Raut, CPM's M A Baby, CPI's D Raja, JMM's Mahua Majhi, NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and IUML's E T Mohammed Basheer.The opposition leaders sought a suspension of SIR without challenging its legality. They also called for eligible voters to be included in the electoral rolls of Punjab and other poll-bound states.After the CJI declined to meet the opposition delegation, Rahul said, "We respect CJI and SC. We are quite happy he has given us a path forward. To tell us we can file a petition is a path forward."The petition also sought the formation of an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge and assisted by technical experts and other eminent citizens. The panel would be tasked with conducting an independent audit, within a fixed timeframe, of deletions and changes made to electoral rolls during SIR.The plea further requested the court to set up a panel to "examine integrity of electoral-roll databases and SIR rollout".Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: KOCHI: Police investigating the fatal Mini Cooper crash near Kochi airport have found videos purportedly showing 19-year-old Suhail Sajeev driving the luxury car at speeds exceeding 200kmph on multiple occasions. One earlier Instagram clip showed the car’s speedometer climbing from 204kmph to 220kmph.Teen driver, three others arrestedSuhail was arrested on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. articles.body: KOCHI: Ernakulam rural police have arrested all four occupants of a Mini Cooper that rammed a scooter on Airport Road in Kerala’s Nedumbassery on Sunday, killing three people. Police suspect the car was travelling at more than 120kmph when the collision occurred.Two more occupants, Ameen Sha (19) and Joyal S Anto (19), both from Alappuzha, were arrested on Monday. The driver, Suhail Sajeev (19), son of Sajeev Jamal, and another passenger, Ninav (19), son of Renjith Kumar, were arrested on Sunday.Police said the driver was booked for negligent driving and culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The other three were booked for abetment, as they allegedly allowed him to drive despite knowing that he was inebriated. All four are college students.Old Instagram video shows speedometer reaching 220kmphAn old Instagram video, posted on April 20 this year on an account purportedly belonging to Suhail Sajeev, shows the Mini Cooper’s speedometer climbing to 220kmph on what appears to be a highway.The 11.8-second clip shows the speedometer reading 204kmph before the speed continues to rise, reaching 220kmph as the video ends. Loud music can be heard playing inside the vehicle.Police said Suhail’s mother had gifted him the luxury car for his birthday. Investigators also found videos purportedly showing him driving at speeds exceeding 200kmph on several occasions.Victims’ bodies handed over to familiesThe bodies of the three victims — Devika (21), from Wayanad; Gopika (22), from Palakkad; and Iyas (21), from Karnataka — were handed over to their families after autopsy.Police suspect the occupants had consumed alcohol at different bars before the accident. Investigators have collected evidence, including CCTV footage and bills from the establishments.While the preliminary investigation indicated that Suhail was under the influence of alcohol at the time of the crash, the team is awaiting laboratory reports to confirm his blood alcohol level.Excise department registers cases against three barsThe excise department registered occurrence reports on Monday against the licences and managers of three bars in Kadavanthra, Palarivattom and a star hotel in Nedumbassery.The cases were registered following information from the police about the youths allegedly consuming alcohol before the crash. articles.title: Japanese World War II destroyer Teruzuki discovered in 2025, 83 years after sinking; the 134-metre wreck lies 800 metres beneath the Pacific
articles.summary: For more than eight decades, the Japanese destroyer Teruzuki lay hidden beneath the waters off the Solomon Islands, its final resting place unseen by
articles.body: For more than eight decades, the Japanese destroyer Teruzuki lay hidden beneath the waters off the Solomon Islands, its final resting place unseen by modern explorers. That changed in July 2025, when an international research team located the World War II warship on the seabed of Iron Bottom Sound. According to the Ocean Exploration Trust’s Nautilus Live, the vessel was discovered using underwater robots after seafloor mapping identified a promising target. The 134-metre-long destroyer sank in December 1942 during the Guadalcanal campaign. Its discovery has brought renewed attention to a naval battle that claimed thousands of lives and left numerous wrecks beneath the Pacific.The Teruzuki was discovered for the first time since its sinking in 1942The discovery of the Teruzuki offered researchers their first opportunity to examine the Japanese destroyer directly since it sank during the Second World War. In an account published on 12 July 2025, the Ocean Exploration Trust reported that its team aboard the exploration vessel E/V Nautilus had located the wreck in Iron Bottom Sound, off Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands. The discovery came 83 years after the vessel disappeared beneath the waves. The Straits Times also reported the finding on 21 July 2025, describing how the survey team identified the wreck using evidence from its structure and historical records. The discovery was particularly significant because researchers could finally study the vessel’s surviving features rather than relying solely on wartime accounts to understand its final hours.The 134-metre destroyer sank after American torpedo boats attacked itCommissioned in 1942, the Teruzuki was an Akizuki-class destroyer measuring 134 metres in length. According to Nautilus Live, it was designed to protect larger warships, particularly aircraft carriers, from aerial attacks. Its final mission, however, involved escorting supply ships supporting Japanese forces on Guadalcanal. In the early hours of 12 December 1942, American patrol boats intercepted the convoy near Cape Esperance. Two torpedoes struck the destroyer’s stern, damaging its rudder, disabling the ship and starting fires. Most of the crew were rescued or managed to swim ashore, but nine men died as the vessel sank. The Straits Times similarly reported that the ship was immobilised by American torpedoes while escorting vessels carrying food and other supplies to the island.Underwater robots and seafloor mapping helped researchers locate the wreckFinding the Teruzuki required researchers to combine seafloor mapping with remotely operated underwater vehicles. The University of New Hampshire’s uncrewed surface vessel DriX first mapped the seabed and identified a target consistent with the destroyer’s reported sinking location. The exploration team then deployed the remotely operated vehicles Hercules and Atalanta to investigate the site. The Straits Times reported that the main wreck lay approximately 800 metres underwater, while the broken stern was found at a separate location about 200 metres away. Researchers compared the visible damage with survivor testimonies and examined the number and positions of the gun turrets. These details, alongside historical records identifying other sunken Akizuki-class destroyers, helped confirm the vessel’s identity.The wreck lies in Iron Bottom Sound, a major site of Pacific War historyThe Teruzuki rests in Iron Bottom Sound, a stretch of water between Guadalcanal, Savo and the Nggela Islands in the Solomon Islands. According to Nautilus Live, the area witnessed five major naval battles between August and December 1942, resulting in the loss of more than 20,000 lives, 111 naval vessels and 1,450 aircraft. The Straits Times reported that the discovery offers researchers another way to examine the hardships faced by Japanese forces attempting to supply troops on Guadalcanal after losing air superiority in the Pacific. The expedition also demonstrated how modern underwater technology can document maritime heritage without recovering wrecks from the seabed. As Nautilus Live noted, the survey brought researchers face-to-face with a warship that had remained unseen since its wartime sinking.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Not a single drop': AI data centre boom sparks water protests on Indonesian island
articles.summary: Around 300 residents of Indonesia’s Batam island stormed a data centre compound with empty bottles and jerry cans, protesting a water shortage that they
articles.body: Around 300 residents of Indonesia’s Batam island stormed a data centre compound with empty bottles and jerry cans, protesting a water shortage that they say has left their homes without running water for three months amid the island’s growing AI infrastructure boom.According to a BBC report, the protesters gathered at Nongsa Digital Park, accusing data centres of having access to water while residents struggled to secure basic household supplies.Authorities have blamed the shortages on a prolonged dry spell and denied allegations that water meant for households was being diverted to data centres."Not a single drop has come through our taps for the last three months... Our water supply had been reliable until the data centres came," BBC quoted Dewi Susanti, a resident of Bakau Serip village saying.She said residents had been forced to rely on tanker trucks supplying what she described as "dirty, cloudy and smelly" water, adding to household expenses and disrupting daily life.Batam's water utility told the BBC it was working to improve supplies but did not comment on whether data centres were contributing to the shortages.BP Batam, the agency overseeing trade and industry, blamed a prolonged dry spell and denied allegations that water meant for households was being diverted to the facilities.The protests come as Batam faces growing pressure on its freshwater resources. The island's 1.3 million residents depend on rainwater collected in six artificial reservoirs, while a local environmental group's simulations suggest Nongsa reservoir, which supplies Bakau Serip, could dry up within a month if rainfall does not return.The water crisis has intensified concerns over Batam's rapid expansion as a data centre hub, with investment in the sector exceeding $6.7 billion as of mid-2026Authorities have approved 10 data centres on the island, six of them in Nongsa Digital Park, while at least six more projects are under review.Following protests in August and September, Batam authorities instructed companies developing data centres to build their own desalination plants rather than rely on freshwater from reservoirs.Why AI data centres need large amounts of freshwaterAI data centres require large amounts of water to cool powerful servers and GPUs that generate heat while processing data. Many facilities use evaporative cooling systems, in which water absorbs heat and evaporates, requiring a continuous supply of fresh water.A typical data centre can consume around 300,000 US gallons (approximately 11.4 lakh litres) of water daily, equivalent to the daily water use of about 1,000 US households. However, consumption varies depending on the facility's size, cooling technology and operating conditions.Beyond direct cooling, data centres also have an indirect water footprint because electricity generation can require water.You use AI every day. articles.title: When Mark Zuckerberg put a $100 billion cheque in the hands of Meta's highest-paid employee Alexandr Wang and asked: Are you sure this is going to...
articles.summary: Mark Zuckerberg has revealed the moment he nearly second-guessed the biggest bet of his career.
articles.body: Mark Zuckerberg has revealed the moment he nearly second-guessed the biggest bet of his career. Appearing on the Cheeky Pint podcast with Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang, the Meta CEO recalled weighing the spending ahead and putting a blunt question to Wang. "We're gonna write this cheque for like a hundred billion dollars or two hundred billion dollars," Zuckerberg said. "I'm like, 'Alex, you sure this is gonna work?'"Wang didn't pretend he was. The Scale AI founder, who now runs Meta Superintelligence Labs, said that towards the end of 2025 he had little more than "a vibe report" on research progress and "some plots" to back it up. "I was feeling good about it, but it was certainly not clear at all that it was going to work," he admitted. The admission comes just as Meta has unveiled Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, the most capable AI models to come out of Wang's lab so far.Meta CFO Susan Li warned Wang that a failed AI model would hit hardThe pressure wasn't only coming from Zuckerberg. Wang recalled a Meta leadership offsite in Hawaii at the end of last year, where the whole executive team had gathered. On the Cheeky Pint episode, he said CFO Susan Li pulled him aside "many times" with the same warning."I just want to tell you if this doesn't work, this is going to be really, really bad. It's going to be very, very bad in financial terms," Wang said, recalling Li's words. "If it's good, it's all good. We're great. But if it's bad, it's really, really, really bad."Zuckerberg didn't push back when Wang joked that Li had scared him a bit too. He put it down to the reality of starting a frontier AI lab from scratch, where "the ante is extremely high." Among the executives, Wang added, the running joke was simply that they hoped it would all work out.The $14.3 billion Scale AI deal made Wang the face of Meta's AI resetWang's arrival was a gamble in itself. After Llama 4 fell flat with developers in April 2025, Zuckerberg paid $14.3 billion for a 49% stake in Scale AI that June and brought Wang in to lead the new lab. Wang reportedly received around $5 billion as part of the deal.The first year was rocky. Muse Spark, released in April as Meta's first proprietary foundation model, drew a lukewarm response from developers, with one startup CEO dismissing it as a "yawn". Meta's stock spent much of the year near the bottom of the megacap pack, and around 8,000 jobs were cut in May. The ad business kept the company steady, with first-quarter revenue up 33% to $56.3 billion.Muse app and Muse Wonder models show Meta's AI bet is gaining groundThe mood shifted in September. Meta's Muse AI agent app climbed to the top of Apple's App Store, crossing 2.8 million downloads in its first 12 days across the US and Canada, according to Sensor Tower. It also set a US daily record of 264,000 downloads on September 19. Days later at Meta Connect, the company showed off Muse Charm, a pocket device built purely for voice chats with the agent.On Monday came Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full. Meta says both scored nearly as well as Anthropic's most advanced models on reasoning, writing and coding tests, though those numbers come from its own data. Muse Wonder Full is limited to subscribers of Meta's Muse Code tool, while Muse Wonder is also available through the Meta Model API. Internally codenamed Watermelon, the models were held back after Meta paused pre-training in July. Zuckerberg teased them over the weekend on an Instagram livestream, while barbecuing.Wang once called Muse Spark an "appetizer" for bigger models. Those models are here now, and he has more than a vibe report to show his boss. Whether they earn back a cheque that size is the question Susan Li will keep asking.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2019, Kanye West bought a $14.495 million Wyoming ranch spanning 6,713 acres, with luxury lodges, helicopter landing pads with almost 2,000 elk in the wilderness
articles.summary: In 2019, Kanye West purchased a $14.495 million Wyoming ranch spanning 6,713 acres, adding a vast mountain estate to his growing property portfolio.
articles.body: In 2019, Kanye West purchased a $14.495 million Wyoming ranch spanning 6,713 acres, adding a vast mountain estate to his growing property portfolio. Known as Bighorn Mountain Ranch, the sprawling retreat featured multiple log lodges, woodland cabins, heated helicopter landing pads and streams running through rugged canyons. Its appeal extended beyond luxury accommodation, with promotional material describing the surrounding wilderness as habitat for approximately 2,000 elk that moved between the ranch and neighbouring public land. The acquisition also reflected West’s wider ambitions in Wyoming, where he had spoken about developing land and creating communities beyond his established life in California.Inside the 6,713-acre Wyoming ranch Kanye West bought for $14.495 millionIn November 2019, Architectural Digest reported that Kanye West had acquired a second Wyoming ranch for $14.495 million, shortly after the purchase of another property in the state. The deal added to the couple’s growing connection with Wyoming, where West had spoken publicly about his interest in developing land and establishing a more permanent base.The second property was known as Bighorn Mountain Ranch. Its history stretched back to 1906, and its 6,713 acres included a varied landscape of canyons, bluffs, mountain country and waterways. Rather than being a single residence surrounded by grounds, the estate contained several groups of buildings spread across the land. Its scale meant that the purchase involved considerably more than a large house, with the terrain and existing facilities forming much of its appeal.Five-bedroom lodge, woodland cabins and helicopter access at the Wyoming ranchOne of the principal residences was a log house called The Lodge at Bald Ridge. The five-bedroom property had four bathrooms and overlooked a pond and canyon. Inside, it included a commercial kitchen, while a wraparound deck and wood-burning fireplace added to its traditional mountain-lodge character.Another accommodation complex, Snowshoe Lodge, stood elsewhere on the estate, with several smaller log cabins nearby. The lodge included a wet bar in its basement, and the property also offered walk-in saunas intended for use during the colder months. The buildings provided different places to stay across the ranch rather than concentrating all the accommodation in one main house.The facilities reflected the demands of a property covering thousands of acres. Visitors and residents could move between separate buildings, while the surrounding landscape provided space for outdoor activities. The ranch also had two heated helicopter landing pads, allowing access by air throughout the year. Greybull, the nearest town mentioned in the property report, was roughly a 10-minute helicopter flight away.Around 2,000 elk used the ranch and neighbouring public landWildlife was another feature of the property. As reported Bighorn Mountain Ranch described the area as habitat used by approximately 2,000 elk. The animals were reported to move between the private estate and adjoining public land, making the wider landscape important to understanding their presence. The animals' use of neighbouring public land also means the number cannot be taken as a measure of wildlife contained entirely within the privately owned acreage.The landscape offered other opportunities for wildlife watching and outdoor recreation. White Creek ran through the ranch, providing a setting for small-trout fishing, while the surrounding canyons and mountain terrain gave the estate much of its distinctive character. These natural features were part of what separated Bighorn Mountain Ranch from a conventional luxury residential property.Kanye West had spoken about building a future in WyomingThe acquisition came as West was discussing ambitions that extended beyond owning a rural retreat. In an interview with radio personality Charlamagne tha God earlier in 2019, he described property development as a direction he wanted to pursue, referring to plans to create communities and develop cities.Kim Kardashian also spoke about West's attachment to the state during a September 2019 appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. She described moving to Wyoming as a long-held dream of his. The comments helped place the ranch purchases within a broader interest in spending time away from the couple's established life in California.West's public statements did not, by themselves, establish that every development idea would be carried out on Bighorn Mountain Ranch. They did, however, show that his interest in Wyoming involved more than acquiring a second home. At the time, he was presenting land ownership and development as part of his longer-term ambitions.A vast rural estate with a different kind of valueBighorn Mountain Ranch combined residential facilities with a large tract of land used by wildlife and suited to outdoor pursuits. Its cabins, lodges and helicopter pads offered a level of private access associated with high-value rural estates, while its streams, open terrain and connections to neighbouring public land gave it a different character from an urban property.The reported purchase price of $14.495 million reflected the scale of the estate and the facilities already in place. Its 6,713 acres were also a defining feature, particularly given the reported movement of elk across the ranch and adjacent public land.The property became part of the public record of Kardashian and West's Wyoming investments in 2019. The report documented the acquisition and described the estate's features at that time.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Divers recovered a bell, signal light and binoculars from Titanic’s sister ship after more than a century underwater
articles.summary: More than a century after the HMHS Britannic sank in the Aegean Sea during the First World War, a team of specialist divers has recovered several objects
articles.body: More than a century after the HMHS Britannic sank in the Aegean Sea during the First World War, a team of specialist divers has recovered several objects from the wreck, including a lookout bell, a navigation light and a pair of binoculars. The operation, conducted in May 2025 with approval from Greece’s Ministry of Culture, marked the first time selected artefacts had been brought to the surface from the ship. According to the Greek Ministry of Culture’s Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities, the recovered objects are undergoing conservation before their planned public display in Greece.What did divers recover from Titanic’s sister ship BritannicThe most notable discoveries include the ship’s observatory bell, a red navigation light from its port side and a pair of observation binoculars. Divers also recovered a porcelain washbasin, detached ceramic tiles from the Turkish bath, silver-plated serving trays and equipment associated with the ship’s first- and second-class accommodation.The Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities, which published its findings from the 2025 research expedition on 15 September 2025, confirmed that these objects were among the items successfully brought up from the wreck. The recovery offered a rare opportunity to preserve objects that had remained underwater since the ship’s sinking in November 1916.The discoveries are significant because they represent different aspects of life aboard Britannic, from the practical equipment used to operate the vessel to the fittings and personal items associated with its passengers.How did Britannic become a hospital ship during the First World WarBritannic was built by the White Star Line as one of its Olympic-class ocean liners, alongside Titanic and Olympic. It was launched in 1914 and was slightly larger and newer than Titanic, according to Popular Mechanics. However, the outbreak of the First World War changed the ship’s intended role before it could establish itself as a passenger liner.The British Admiralty requisitioned Britannic and converted it into a hospital ship. Designated HMHS Britannic, it was used to transport and care for wounded servicemen during the conflict.On 16 November 1916, while travelling off the Greek island of Kea towards the hospital station on Lemnos, the vessel struck a German mine. The Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities states that the ship sank in less than an hour.There were 1,065 people aboard, and 30 died when two lifeboats were swept into the ship’s still-turning propellers. Although the loss of life was tragic, most people on board survived.The circumstances of the sinking gave Britannic a different history from Titanic, which sank after striking an iceberg in April 1912. Both ships belonged to the same famous liner family, but Britannic’s final voyage was shaped by the demands of wartime medical service.The underwater recovery was very challengingThe wreck lies more than 120 metres below the surface of the Aegean Sea, close to Kea. Popular Mechanics describes the site as roughly 400 feet deep and about 45 miles south-east of Athens. Its depth, strong currents and poor visibility make exploration difficult and restrict access to specialist divers.The May 2025 expedition involved an 11-member team of professional deep-sea divers. British historian Simon Mills, founder of the Britannic Foundation, organised the research, while experienced diving specialists managed the safety and practical arrangements. Greece’s Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities supervised the operation and oversaw the handling of the recovered objects.According to the Ephorate, the divers used closed-circuit diving equipment to work at the wreck. These systems recycle breathing gas rather than releasing every breath directly into the water, making them suitable for specialised deep dives.Even with careful planning, the team could not recover every object identified in advance. The official report explains that the condition and position of certain items prevented their removal. Strong currents, limited visibility and the fragile state of the wreck added to the difficulties.The expedition therefore focused on selected objects that could be retrieved safely, rather than attempting to remove everything of interest from the site.How were the recovered objects brought to the surfaceThe divers used specially designed lift bags to raise the selected artefacts from the seabed. Once recovered, the objects were placed in protective containers, and cleaning began to remove marine organisms that had accumulated on their surfaces.Good News Network reported that the objects were secured for transfer to a conservation centre in Athens. The Ephorate’s account provides further details, explaining that the items were initially stored in a space provided by the Ephorate with assistance from the Kea Police Department.They were subsequently transferred to the Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities’ laboratories in Athens, where conservation work is continuing.This stage is essential because removing an object from the sea does not automatically make it suitable for display. After more than a century underwater, artefacts can carry marine growth and may require careful treatment to preserve their remaining material and details.Where will Britannic’s recovered artefacts be displayedThe objects are intended to become part of the permanent exhibition at the National Museum of Underwater Antiquities, which is under construction in Piraeus, Greece. According to the Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities, the artefacts will feature in the museum’s section devoted to the First World War, where Britannic’s wreck will be a prominent exhibit.The planned display will bring together objects recovered from the ship and help visitors understand its role during the conflict. The bell and navigation light reflect the equipment needed to operate a large vessel, while the washbasin, serving trays and Turkish bath tiles offer a glimpse of its onboard facilities. The recovered binoculars also provide a tangible connection to the people who travelled or worked aboard the ship before it sank.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: BMC issues show-cause notice to Mumbai Coastal Road contractors over unauthorised debris use
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Days after the BMC launched the Mumbai Debris Control and Tracking System (MDCTS) portal to track C&D waste from the site where it is generated to
articles.body: MUMBAI: Days after the BMC launched the Mumbai Debris Control and Tracking System (MDCTS) portal to track C&D waste from the site where it is generated to an authorised unloading site, the BMC has issued a show-cause notice to the contractors executing a package of the Mumbai Coastal Road (south) project over the alleged use of excavation material sourced from private construction sites without mandatory transportation permissions.The civic body has directed the Larsen & Toubro-HCC joint venture to stop backfilling work using unauthorised material until clearance is obtained from the civic administration. The contractor has been given 72 hours to explain why the material should not be removed at its cost and stringent action initiated against it.A senior BMC official said, “The objective is for BMC to improve accountability by linking construction and demolition waste from its source and upto its final destination.”Staring October 12, BMC has also begun imposing a ₹25,000 penalty per violation on vehicles transporting construction and excavation waste without an authorised, active tracking system.Meanwhile the notice follows a site inspection conducted by the BMC’s solid waste management department on October 1 at the coastal stretch between Haji Ali and PDP Garden. Officials found backfilling activity underway and, upon checking vehicle details and challans, found that the earth being used was reportedly being brought from private building construction sites across Mumbai.According to the notice, the developers and transporters concerned had not obtained the mandatory permission to transport excavation material from the BMC or the competent authority. The civic body said the use of material from unauthorised sources violated the tender conditions, which require filling material to be procured only from authorised quarries or approved sources with valid permissions.The notice cites violations of the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules of 2016 and 2025, directions of the Bombay high court concerning illegal transportation of earth and debris, and the project’s contractual conditions and technical specifications.The contractor has been asked to submit supporting documents, including details of the source of the material, valid transportation permissions, royalty challans and geotechnical test reports. It must also provide a statement of the material brought to the site, along with details of approved sources.BMC has warned that failure to submit a satisfactory reply within the stipulated period could lead to further action without additional notice. The civic body has also directed its officials to initiate action against private developers found transporting construction and demolition material without the required permission.A response from L & T spokesperson stated, “We have received the notice from the BMC’s Solid Waste Management department regarding the source of backfilling material at a section of the Mumbai Coastal Road project. Compliance with all applicable rules, permissions and contract conditions is a priority for us. We remain committed to resolving this matter promptly and to delivering the project to the required standards.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news.
