articles.title: Man's fatal fall from Six Flags roller coaster sparks horrifying eyewitness accounts
articles.summary: Witnesses give accounts of a man falling to his death at Six Flags in Georgia. The company has temporarily closed similar roller coasters at multiple parks after the incident on the Goliath ride.
articles.body: Witnesses described horrifying scenes after a man reportedly fell to his death from a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia — leaving other passengers stranded high above the ground. The man was riding the roller coaster with his son, while his wife and daughter watched from the ground, according to an eyewitness account reported by local station WXIA. The incident occurred around 4 p.m. Monday on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. TERRIFYING SCENE UNFOLDS AT SIX FLAGS AS STORM-TOPPLED TREE SENDS 4 GUESTS TO HOSPITAL One witness told local outlet WXIA the man appeared in a souvenir photo taken during the ride. "He was in our pictures," the witness said. "He fell and hit the car three different times." Fox News Digital reached out to Six Flags for the latest on the ride's status. Another couple who were on the ride described the terrifying moments surrounding the man's death, according to WXIA. "The vehicle [meaning the ride] hit him, and then he flew back up again, and it hit him again, and then that's when he was, I guess, flung from the ride," the man told the outlet. "It went from having a great time to just screaming, 'Oh my God, what is happening,'" his wife said. "You don't see things like this happen. It should never happen." FRIGHTENING SCENE UNFOLDS ON ICONIC SKY RIDE AS CHILD FALLS DOWN ONTO BOARDWALK Meanwhile, another Goliath rider said his train was ascending when passengers heard screaming and saw people running below. The ride then stopped, leaving them stranded for about an hour without updates. "We were up there for an hour with no updates, no news, no nothing. We just saw everyone running out of the park," the witness told WXIA. "We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today." The Cobb County Police Department previously confirmed to Fox News Digital that one person died, and several others were reportedly injured. Police did not immediately provide further details about the circumstances surrounding the incident. "We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," a Six Flags spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital. WOMAN ALLEGEDLY EJECTED FROM ROLLER COASTER, SUFFERS SERIOUS INJURIES AFTER DRAGGED ALONG TRACK: REPORTS "Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected." Following the incident, Six Flags temporarily closed similar attractions at other parks as a precaution, the company confirmed to local outlet WSB-TV. "Out of an abundance of caution, we have temporarily closed similar attractions across our parks," a Six Flags spokesperson said, according to the outlet. "The safety of our guests and team members remains one of our highest priorities." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER As of Tuesday morning, it was unclear which rides were temporarily closed. Six Flags Magic Mountain in California and Six Flags Great America in Illinois also have roller coasters named Goliath, though the attractions feature different designs. Coaster scrutiny The incident comes as Six Flags has been facing scrutiny over another roller coaster at its Magic Mountain park in California. Six Flags Magic Mountain permanently closed its X2 roller coaster after multiple lawsuits accused the attraction of causing catastrophic brain injuries. A spokesperson for Six Flags Magic Mountain confirmed earlier to Fox News Digital that X2 had not operated since July 12. Dordick Law Corporation of Beverly Hills, which represents the plaintiffs, said it has retained more than 100 additional clients who allege they suffered brain injuries after riding X2, the firm told Fox News Digital on Sept. 23. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS So far, three lawsuits have been filed. Magic Mountain Park President Brian Oerding said the coaster consistently passed safety tests, but the park decided to close it amid concerns about guest confidence. "While X2 consistently passed a multitude of safety tests, we have decided to close the ride because we believe it’s the right thing to do," Oerding said in a statement. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Ride safety is a cornerstone of our business, and when we see guest confidence affected, we take it seriously." A Six Flags spokesperson previously declined to comment on pending litigation. The allegations have not yet been adjudicated, and Six Flags will have an opportunity to respond in court. articles.title: Vacant bingo hall to become immersive Elstree film experience
articles.summary: A lease is secured for a new visitor attraction near Elstree Studios.
articles.body:
A lease has been secured to transform a vacant bingo hall into an "immersive experience" where visitors can become a film crew.

The contract is for a 23,000-square-foot space in The Point on Borehamwood High Street in Hertfordshire, close to the famous Elstree Studios.

The Elstree Immersive Experience project is funded by Hertsmere Council with £2m from the Community Infrastructure Levy and £1.3m in external investment.

According to the council, the venue will be "dedicated to an ever-changing range of hands-on, multi-sensory experiences carefully designed to have broad appeal to every demographic".

Managing director Adam Morley described the venue as a "playground for content creation for all the family".

He said visitors would be able to select a film or television genre and direct, star in, or crew their own production before attending an on-site film premiere.

The venue will also house an animation zone where visitors can interact with holographic characters.

Morley said the experience would include an archive reflecting on a century of local film-making, celebrating the studio's involvement with titles such as Star Wars, EastEnders and Strictly Come Dancing.

He added: "How do we regenerate High Streets? How do we get footfall back in? Well, this is one of the ways of doing that."

"How many vape shops and barbers have you got, when actually we could bring something like this to every High Street in the UK to tell the story of that location?"

The attraction is scheduled to open in spring 2027.

articles.title: US ambassador to Greece resigns amid misconduct allegations
articles.summary: Kimberly Guilfoyle denies allegations that she offered access to Trump administration officials in exchange for money.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump’s Ambassador to Greece, Kimberley Guilfoyle, has resigned following a series of allegations of misconduct, including claims that she offered a political donor access to senior administration officials in exchange for money.

“We have asked ambassador Guilfoyle to resign,” White House press secretary Katie Zacharia told reporters earlier on Tuesday. “She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well.”

The announcement comes after weeks of damaging reports about Guilfoyle’s conduct.

Shortly after Zacharia’s comments, Guilfoyle posted on social media that she was resigning.

“While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end,” she wrote.

She also denied the allegations against her.

“These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity,” she said.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Guilfoyle asked a Trump donor to cover a $100,000 credit card bill shortly before her congressional confirmation hearing, promising him access to administration officials in return.

The newspaper also reported that she told guests at a reception that she could use US influence to undermine the Greek government, promoted the interests of a Greek construction and energy company, and allowed one of its lobbyists to attend private diplomatic meetings.

Guilfoyle’s lawyers have said the money she sought was payment for previous speaking engagements and public appearances that she had not received.

Trump had signalled on Monday that he was considering removing her from the post.

“Well, we’re looking at it,” he told reporters. “We’re not happy.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio initially defended Guilfoyle, calling her a “strong ambassador,” but later declined to comment on the allegations and criticised reporters for asking about them.

Guilfoyle is a former Fox News host and California prosecutor. She is the former wife of California Governor Gavin Newsom and was previously engaged to Trump’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr.
